- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.7) — reduce forecast slightly to avoid overreaction.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.3) — increase forecast modestly to account for potential rebound.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes in sentiment — cap forecast peak at 1–2% below true peak to avoid overcorrection.
- Lagging forecasts often underestimate near-term moves — adjust early forecast to align with recent sentiment momentum.
- Mean-reversion bias in long-term forecasts — if 30d forecast is >10% above recent 18d average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- Sentiment drop after spike → forecast should not continue upward — reduce slope or add downward bias if sentiment <0.5 for 3+ days.
- Forecast should not exceed 15% above or below 18d moving average unless sentiment strongly diverges (e.g., >0.9 or <0.1).
